title: Python
label: Python
desc: General-purpose language with readable syntax and a large standard library.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Check the interpreter and run a first script.

snippets.code:
# Check the interpreter that answers to python3
python3 --version

# Confirm pip is available for that interpreter
python3 -m pip --version

# Install a package for the current interpreter
python3 -m pip install requests

# Run a file, then drop into the interactive REPL
python3 hello.py
python3

sections.title: Basic Syntax
sections.description: Comments, indentation and statement layout.

snippets.code:
# Comments start with a hash
print("Hello, world")  # trailing comment

# Indentation defines blocks; four spaces is the convention
if True:
    print("inside the block")
print("outside the block")

# A backslash joins a long statement onto the next line
total = 1 + 2 + \
        3
print(total)  # 6

# A module docstring documents the file
"""Small helpers for the demo."""

# Semicolons can separate statements but are rarely needed
x = 1; y = 2

# Expressions in the REPL echo their value
# >>> 2 ** 10
# 1024

sections.title: Variables
sections.description: Bind names to values and rebind them freely.

snippets.code:
name = "Ada"
age = 36
height = 1.68
is_admin = False

# Names are bound to objects; the type comes from the value
print(type(age))  # <class 'int'>

# Several targets at once, including a swap
x, y = 10, 20
x, y = y, x
print(x, y)  # 20 10

# A name can be rebound to a different type
value = 42
value = "forty-two"
print(value)  # forty-two

# Constants are a naming convention, not a language rule
MAX_RETRIES = 3

# del removes the binding, not the object itself
temp = [1, 2, 3]
del temp

# Augmented assignment updates in place when possible
count = 0
count += 1
count *= 5
print(count)  # 5

sections.title: Types
sections.description: Built-in scalars, conversion and type checks.

snippets.code:
count = 42
ratio = 0.5
flag = True
nothing = None

print(type(count))    # <class 'int'>
print(type(ratio))    # <class 'float'>
print(type(flag))     # <class 'bool'>
print(type(nothing))  # <class 'NoneType'>

# Explicit conversions
print(int("17"))     # 17
print(float("2.5"))  # 2.5
print(str(99))       # 99
print(bool(0))       # False
print(bool("text"))  # True

# isinstance follows subclass relationships
print(isinstance(True, int))  # True: bool is a subclass of int

# Integers have arbitrary precision
print(2 ** 100)
# 1267650600228229401496703205376

sections.title: Strings
sections.description: Format, slice and transform text.

snippets.code:
name = "Ada"
role = "engineer"

# f-strings embed expressions directly
print(f"{name} is an {role}")               # Ada is an engineer
print(f"{name!r} has {len(name)} letters")  # 'Ada' has 3 letters

# Slicing: start, stop, step
text = "python"
print(text[0])     # p
print(text[-1])    # n
print(text[1:4])   # yth
print(text[::-1])  # nohtyp

# Common methods return new strings
line = "  Hello, World  "
print(line.strip())          # Hello, World
print(line.strip().lower())  # hello, world
print("a,b,c".split(","))    # ['a', 'b', 'c']
print("-".join(["a", "b"]))  # a-b
print("python".replace("py", "Py"))  # Python

# Raw strings ignore escapes; triple quotes span lines
path = r"C:\Users\ada\notes"
query = """SELECT id
FROM users
WHERE active = 1"""
print(path)
print(query)

sections.title: Lists
sections.description: Ordered, mutable sequences with slicing and in-place methods.

snippets.code:
numbers = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]

print(numbers[0])   # 3
print(numbers[-1])  # 5
print(numbers[1:3]) # [1, 4]

# Append, extend, insert
numbers.append(9)       # [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9]
numbers.extend([2, 6])  # [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6]
numbers.insert(0, 0)    # [0, 3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6]
print(numbers)

# Sorting in place versus a sorted copy
values = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
values.sort()
print(values)  # [1, 1, 3, 4, 5]

words = ["pear", "fig", "apple"]
print(sorted(words, key=len))  # ['fig', 'pear', 'apple']
print(words)                   # original order is unchanged

# Remove by value or by position
values.remove(1)     # drops the first 1
last = values.pop()  # 5
print(values, last)  # [1, 3, 4] 5

# Lists are mutable and aliases share the same object
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
b.append(4)
print(a)  # [1, 2, 3, 4]

# copy() or a full slice makes a shallow copy
c = a.copy()
c.append(5)
print(a, c)  # [1, 2, 3, 4] [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

sections.title: Dictionaries
sections.description: Key-value maps with fast lookup and insertion order.

snippets.code:
user = {"name": "Ada", "age": 36, "city": "London"}

print(user["name"])                  # Ada
print(user.get("email"))             # None
print(user.get("email", "unknown"))  # unknown

# Insert and update
user["email"] = "ada@example.com"
user.update({"age": 37, "active": True})
print(user)

# Iterate over keys, values or both
scores = {"math": 90, "art": 75}

for subject in scores:
    print(subject)

for subject, score in scores.items():
    print(subject, score)

# Membership tests keys, not values
print("math" in scores)  # True

# Remove a key and read what it held
art = scores.pop("art")
print(scores, art)  # {'math': 90} 75

sections.title: Sets and Tuples
sections.description: Unique unordered values and immutable records.

snippets.code:
# Tuples are immutable and hashable when their items are
point = (3.5, -1.2)
x, y = point
print(x, y)  # 3.5 -1.2

single = (42,)       # trailing comma makes a one-item tuple
print(type(single))  # <class 'tuple'>

# Tuples can be dictionary keys; lists cannot
locations = {(0, 0): "origin", (1, 2): "target"}
print(locations[(1, 2)])  # target

# frozenset is an immutable set and can also be a key
permissions = frozenset({"read", "write"})
print("read" in permissions)  # True

# Unpacking with a star collects the rest
first, *middle, last = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print(first, middle, last)  # 1 [2, 3, 4] 5

sections.title: Control Flow
sections.description: Branches, loops and pattern matching.

snippets.code:
# for/else runs else when the loop was not broken
for item in [2, 4, 6]:
    if item % 2:
        print("odd found")
        break
else:
    print("all even")  # all even

# match compares against patterns, not just values
command = ("move", 3, 4)
match command:
    case ("quit",):
        print("bye")
    case ("move", x, y):
        print(f"moving to {x},{y}")
    case _:
        print("unknown")

sections.title: Comprehensions
sections.description: Build collections and lazy sequences in one expression.

snippets.code:
# List comprehension: expression first, then the loop
squares = [n * n for n in range(6)]
print(squares)  # [0, 1, 4, 9, 16, 25]

# Add a filter
evens = [n for n in range(10) if n % 2 == 0]
print(evens)  # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]

# Nested loops read left to right
pairs = [(x, y) for x in range(2) for y in range(2)]
print(pairs)  # [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]

# A generator expression is lazy and keeps memory flat
total = sum(n * n for n in range(1_000_000))
print(total)  # 333332833333500000

# Parentheses around a generator can be dropped inside a call
lines = ["  one ", " two  "]
cleaned = list(s.strip() for s in lines)
print(cleaned)  # ['one', 'two']

sections.title: Functions
sections.description: Parameters, defaults, variadic arguments and first-class callables.

snippets.code:
def greet(name: str, greeting: str = "Hello") -> str:
    """Return a greeting for name."""
    return f"{greeting}, {name}!"

print(greet("Ada"))                       # Hello, Ada!
print(greet("Ada", greeting="Hi"))        # Hi, Ada!
print(greet(name="Ada", greeting="Hey"))  # Hey, Ada!

# *args collects extra positional arguments, **kwargs extra keywords
def report(*values, **options):
    label = options.get("label", "values")
    print(label, values)

report(1, 2, 3)                # values (1, 2, 3)
report(1, 2, label="numbers")  # numbers (1, 2)

# Unpacking at the call site spreads a list or dict
args = [4, 5]
kwargs = {"label": "pair"}
report(*args, **kwargs)  # pair (4, 5)

# Functions are objects: assign, pass and return them
def double(x):
    return x * 2

def apply(func, value):
    return func(value)

print(apply(double, 21))  # 42

# lambda is a short anonymous function
add = lambda a, b: a + b
print(add(2, 3))  # 5

# A common pattern: sort by a computed key
people = [("Ada", 36), ("Alan", 41)]
print(sorted(people, key=lambda person: person[1]))
# [('Ada', 36), ('Alan', 41)]

sections.title: Classes
sections.description: Define objects with state, behaviour and inheritance.

snippets.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

# Dataclasses generate __init__, __repr__ and __eq__
@dataclass
class Point:
    x: float
    y: float
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def distance_to_origin(self) -> float:
        return (self.x ** 2 + self.y ** 2) ** 0.5


p = Point(3.0, 4.0)
p.tags.append("corner")
print(p)                     # Point(x=3.0, y=4.0, tags=['corner'])
print(p.distance_to_origin())  # 5.0

sections.title: Files
sections.description: Read and write text with open or pathlib.

snippets.code:
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("notes.txt")

# Write text, replacing the file
path.write_text("first line\nsecond line\n", encoding="utf-8")

# Read the whole file at once
print(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

# with closes the file even when an error occurs
with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    handle.write("alpha\n")
    handle.write("beta\n")

with open("notes.txt", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    for line in handle:
        print(line.rstrip())  # alpha / beta

from pathlib import Path

# Walk a directory and filter with glob patterns
root = Path(".")
for path in sorted(root.glob("*.txt")):
    print(path.name, path.stat().st_size)

# Build paths without string concatenation
data_dir = Path("data") / "topics"
print(data_dir)        # data/topics
print(data_dir.exists())

sections.title: JSON
sections.description: Encode and decode JSON strings and files.

snippets.code:
import json

payload = {"name": "Ada", "age": 36, "tags": ["math", "code"]}

# Compact and pretty serialization
text = json.dumps(payload)
print(text)

pretty = json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
print(pretty)

# Parse a string back into Python objects
loaded = json.loads(text)
print(loaded["tags"][0])  # math

import json
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("config.json")
data = {"host": "localhost", "port": 8080, "debug": False}

with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    json.dump(data, handle, indent=2)

with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    restored = json.load(handle)

print(restored["port"])  # 8080

sections.title: Modules and Imports
sections.description: Split code across modules and packages.

snippets.code:
# Import the whole module
import math
print(math.sqrt(16))  # 4.0

# Import a name, optionally with an alias
from math import ceil, floor
from statistics import mean as average

print(ceil(2.1), floor(2.9))  # 3 2
print(average([1, 2, 3]))     # 2

# helpers.py
def double(x):
    return x * 2

# Only run the demo when this file is executed directly
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(double(21))  # 42

# In another file:
# import helpers
# print(helpers.double(5))  # 10

# Inside a package, prefer absolute imports
# project/app/main.py
from app.services import load_config

# Relative imports work within the same package
from .services import load_config

# Find where a module lives
import json
print(json.__file__)

sections.title: Testing
sections.description: Write and run automated checks with unittest or pytest.

snippets.code:
# Run every test in the current directory
python3 -m unittest discover -v

# Run a single module or a single test case
python3 -m unittest test_calculator
python3 -m unittest test_calculator.TestAdd.test_adds_integers

# test_calculator.py in pytest style
import pytest

from calculator import add


def test_adds_integers():
    assert add(2, 3) == 5


def test_rejects_bad_input():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        add("2", 3)

sections.title: Virtual Environments
sections.description: Isolate dependencies per project with venv and pip.

snippets.code:
# Create an isolated environment in .venv
python3 -m venv .venv

# Activate it (Bash or Zsh)
source .venv/bin/activate
python --version
which python   # the interpreter inside .venv

# Leave the environment
deactivate

# Install and record dependencies
python -m pip install requests==2.32.3
python -m pip freeze > requirements.txt

# Recreate the environment elsewhere
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

# Show what is installed
python -m pip list

sections.title: Standard Library Essentials
sections.description: Everyday tools that ship with Python.

snippets.code:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta

words = ["red", "blue", "red", "green", "red"]
print(Counter(words).most_common(2))  # [('red', 3), ('blue', 1)]

groups = defaultdict(list)
groups["fruit"].append("apple")
print(dict(groups))  # {'fruit': ['apple']}

today = date(2026, 11, 4)
print(today + timedelta(days=10))  # 2026-11-14

import itertools
import random

print(list(itertools.islice(itertools.count(10, 5), 3)))  # [10, 15, 20]
print(list(itertools.combinations("abc", 2)))
# [('a', 'b'), ('a', 'c'), ('b', 'c')]

random.seed(7)
print(random.choice(["rock", "paper", "scissors"]))
print(random.sample(range(10), 3))

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

text = "order 42 shipped, order 77 pending"
print(re.findall(r"order (\d+)", text))  # ['42', '77']

print(Path.home().name)
print(sys.version_info[:2])

sections.title: Pythonic Idioms
sections.description: Small patterns that make code shorter and clearer.

snippets.code:
# Truthiness: empty containers and None are false
items = []
if not items:
    print("empty")  # empty

# Conditional expression
status = "ok" if items else "empty"
print(status)  # empty

# any and all short-circuit
print(any(n > 5 for n in [1, 9, 3]))  # True
print(all(n > 0 for n in [1, 2, 3]))  # True

# Prefer EAFP over checking first
try:
    value = {"a": 1}["a"]
except KeyError:
    value = 0
print(value)  # 1

# Swap without a temporary
a, b = 1, 2
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)  # 2 1

# Join strings instead of concatenating in a loop
parts = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]
line = ", ".join(parts)
print(line)  # alpha, beta, gamma
